TinkerOS is a custom Linux-based operating system built on a real Linux kernel. It comes with three special modes called worlds, a built-in AI assistant, and over 224 system tools.
TinkerOS has three worlds: Game Station for gaming with max performance, Hackerspace for coding and development, and Normal for everyday use. You can switch between them anytime.
Type tinker-world game for Game Station, tinker-world hack for Hackerspace, or tinker-world normal for Normal mode. You can also select the world at the login screen.
Game Station is TinkerOS's gaming world. It automatically enables Game Mode, sets CPU to maximum performance, optimizes your GPU, and configures controller support. Great for gaming sessions.
Hackerspace is the developer world in TinkerOS. It comes with code editors, terminal tools, Docker, and development environments pre-configured. Perfect for coding and programming.

input: How do I open the Control Center?
output: Type tinkeros-control-center in the terminal or click the TinkerOS logo in the top-left corner of your screen. The Control Center has over 224 tools organized into categories like System, Gaming, Hardware, and more.
Searchie is TinkerOS's personal search engine. It indexes your files, browser history, and documents so you can find anything instantly. Press Tab+F7 to open it, or type searchie in the terminal.

input: How do I search my files?
output: Press Tab+F7 to open Searchie, then type what you're looking for. It searches through all your indexed files and shows results ranked by relevance. You can also use the terminal: searchie ask 'query'.

TinkerAI is your built-in AI assistant, like Siri or Google Assistant but for your computer. Press Ctrl+Alt+Gr to open it, or type tinker-ai ask 'question' in the terminal. It can answer questions, control your computer, and help with tasks.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Gr on your keyboard to open TinkerAI. You can also type tinker-ai ask 'your question' in the terminal. The AI pops up as a glassmorphism overlay at the top of your screen.

input: How do I enable Game Mode?
output: Game Mode is automatic in the Game Station world. To enable it manually, type tinker-gamemode on in the terminal. To check if it's running, type tinker-gamemode status.

input: How do I take a screenshot?
output: Type tinker-ai screenshot in the terminal, or use the standard Print Screen key. The screenshot is saved to your Pictures folder. You can also ask TinkerAI to take one for you.

input: How do I adjust the volume?
output: Use the volume icon in the top-right system tray, or type tinker-audio volume 75 in the terminal to set it to 75%. You can also use the keyboard volume keys.

input: How do I change the brightness?
output: Type tinker-display brightness 80 in the terminal to set brightness to 80%. You can also use the brightness keys on your keyboard, or adjust it in the Control Center under Display settings.

input: How do I open a browser?
output: Type tinker-ai open firefox or tinker-ai open chrome in the terminal. You can also click the browser icon in your taskbar, or ask TinkerAI to open your browser for you.
Type tinker-update in the terminal to check for and install updates. You can also use the Software Center app, or go to Control Center > System > Updates.

input: How do I backup my data?
output: Type tinker-backup in the terminal to start the backup wizard. It will guide you through backing up your important files to an external drive or cloud storage.

input: What kernel modules does TinkerOS have?
output: TinkerOS has custom kernel modules: thermal_sched for smart cooling, gamemode for gaming boost, energy_sched for battery saving, coil_whine for noise reduction, oled_wear for burn-in protection, and cache_tiering for performance.

input: How do I fix WiFi problems?
output: First check: nmcli device status. If WiFi is disconnected, try: nmcli device wifi list to see available networks, then: nmcli device wifi connect 'NetworkName'. If that doesn't work, restart NetworkManager: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager.

input: How do I fix audio problems?
output: Check your audio devices: pactl list sinks. Restart the audio system: pulseaudio -k && pulseaudio --start. To set a default device: pactl set-default-sink device-name. You can also check the Control Center > Sound settings.

input: How do I install new apps?
output: You can install apps through the Software Center, Flatpak, or the terminal. For terminal: sudo apt install package-name. For Flatpak: flatpak install app-name. TinkerOS supports AppImage files too — just download and run them.

input: How do I customize the theme?
output: Open Control Center > Customization. You can change themes, icons, fonts, and the glassmorphism effects. TinkerOS uses a glass design language with frosted glass and blur effects throughout the interface.
Glassmorphism is TinkerOS's visual style — frosted glass panels with transparency, blur effects, rounded corners, and subtle shadows. It gives the desktop a modern, clean, and premium look.

input: How do I set a reminder?
output: Open TinkerAI with Ctrl+Alt+Gr and say or type: remind me to take a break in 30 minutes. You can also use: tinker-ai remind 'message' 30m in the terminal.

input: How do I add a contact?
output: Use TinkerAI: tinker-ai contact-add 'John Doe' '555-1234' 'john@email.com'. You can also manage contacts through the Contacts app in your application menu.

input: How do I check my battery?
output: Look at the battery icon in the top-right system tray for a quick estimate. For detailed info, open Control Center > Hardware > Battery, or type tinker-battery status in the terminal.

input: How do I enable the firewall?
output: Type tinker-firewall enable in the terminal. To check status: tinker-firewall status. You can also configure it through Control Center > Security > Firewall.

input: How do I clean up disk space?
output: Type tinker-cleanup in the terminal. This will remove old packages, clear cache, and clean up temporary files. You can also use Control Center > System > Cleanup for a GUI option.

input: How do I run the dust dislodger?
output: Type tinker-dust run in the terminal. This spins your fans at special intervals to dislodge dust from the vents. It's a maintenance feature to keep your cooling system working well.

The dust dislodger is a unique TinkerOS feature that spins your computer fans at carefully calculated speeds and intervals to shake loose dust from the cooling vents, helping maintain optimal airflow.

input: How do I check system temperature?
output: Type sensors in the terminal to see CPU and GPU temperatures. You can also check through Control Center > Hardware > Temperature. TinkerOS's thermal_sched module manages cooling automatically.

input: How do I switch to dark mode?
output: Open Control Center > Customization > Appearance and select Dark mode. Or type: gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme 'prefer-dark' in the terminal.

input: How do I open a terminal?
output: Right click on the desktop and select 'Open Terminal', or press Ctrl+Alt+T, or search for 'Terminal' in the application menu.
TinkerOS includes a web browser, file manager, text editor, terminal, calculator, media player, email client, calendar, and over 224 system tools. It also has TinkerAI and Searchie built in.

input: How do I add a printer?
output: Open Control Center > Hardware > Printers. Click 'Add Printer' and follow the wizard. TinkerOS supports most USB and network printers automatically.

input: How do I connect Bluetooth devices?
output: Click the Bluetooth icon in the system tray, or open Control Center > Network > Bluetooth. Put your device in pairing mode, then click 'Pair' next to it in the list.

input: How do I set up a VPN?
output: Open Control Center > Network > VPN. Click 'Add VPN' and enter your VPN provider's details. TinkerOS supports OpenVPN, WireGuard, and PPTP protocols.

input: What file system does TinkerOS use?
output: TinkerOS uses ext4 as the default file system, which is the standard for Linux. It's reliable, fast, and well-tested. You can also use btrfs if you prefer snapshot support.

input: How do I resize a partition?
output: Open Control Center > System > Disks, or use GParted. Be careful when resizing partitions — always backup your data first. Select the partition, click Resize, and apply changes.

input: How do I check for updates?
output: Type tinker-update in the terminal, or open the Software Center app. TinkerOS will check for system updates, security patches, and app updates automatically.
Click the system menu in the top-right corner and select Restart, or type sudo reboot in the terminal. You can also press Ctrl+Alt+Delete if configured.

input: How do I shut down TinkerOS?
output: Click the system menu in the top-right corner and select Shut Down, or type sudo shutdown now in the terminal. Hold the power button for 4 seconds as a last resort.

input: How do I create a new user?
output: Open Control Center > System > Users, or type: sudo adduser newusername in the terminal. You can set the password and permissions during creation.

input: How do I change my password?
output: Open Control Center > System > Users > Change Password, or type passwd in the terminal. You'll need to enter your current password first.

input: How do I enable automatic updates?
output: Open Control Center > System > Updates and enable 'Automatic Updates'. You can choose to install security updates automatically while keeping other updates manual.
TinkerOS comes with Python, Bash, and common development tools pre-installed. In the Hackerspace world, you also get Node.js, Rust, Go, and Java environments set up and ready to use.

input: How do I install Python packages?
output: Use pip: pip install package-name. For system-wide installation: sudo pip install package-name. TinkerOS recommends using virtual environments: python -m venv myenv && source myenv/bin/activate.

input: How do I use Docker on TinkerOS?
output: Docker is pre-installed in the Hackerspace world. Start it with: sudo systemctl start docker. Run containers: docker run -it ubuntu bash. Add your user to the docker group: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER.

input: How do I use Git on TinkerOS?
output: Git is pre-configured. Clone a repo: git clone https://github.com/user/repo. Make changes, then: git add . && git commit -m 'message' && git push. TinkerOS has Git configured with sensible defaults.

TinkerOS uses tmux as the terminal multiplexer. It lets you have multiple terminal sessions in one window. Start it with: tmux. Split panes with Ctrl+B then % or ". Navigate with Ctrl+B then arrow keys.
Start tmux with: tmux. Create a new window: Ctrl+B then c. Split horizontally: Ctrl+B then ". Split vertically: Ctrl+B then %. Detach: Ctrl+B then d. Reattach: tmux attach.

input: How do I check my disk usage?
output: Type df -h to see disk usage by partition. Use du -sh foldername to check a specific folder. Open Control Center > System > Storage for a visual overview with cleanup options.

input: How do I check my RAM usage?
output: Type free -h to see RAM usage. Use top or htop for a real-time view. Open Control Center > System > Memory for a visual display of memory usage.

input: How do I check my CPU usage?
output: Type top or htop in the terminal for real-time CPU monitoring. Use lscpu to see CPU info. Open Control Center > Hardware > CPU for a visual display.

input: How do I kill a frozen app?
output: Try Alt+F4 to close the window normally. If that doesn't work, type xkill and click the frozen app. As a last resort, use: killall app-name or: kill $(pgrep app-name).

Try these steps: 1) Check CPU usage with top or htop. 2) Close unused apps. 3) Run tinker-cleanup to free disk space. 4) Restart the computer. 5) Check for overheating with sensors. 6) Switch to Normal world if in Game Station.

Try: 1) Press Ctrl+Alt+F2 to switch to a text terminal. 2) Login and type: sudo systemctl restart gdm3. 3) If that doesn't work, try: sudo apt update && sudo apt reinstall ubuntu-desktop. 4) Check cables if using external monitor.
Check: nmcli device status. Restart network: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager. For WiFi: nmcli device wifi list && nmcli device wifi connect 'SSID'. For ethernet: check cable connection.
TinkerOS supports full disk encryption during installation. For individual files, use: gpg -c filename to encrypt, gpg filename.gpg to decrypt. You can also use VeraCrypt for encrypted volumes.

input: How do I scan for viruses?
output: TinkerOS includes ClamAV. Scan with: sudo clamscan -r /home. For real-time protection, enable ClamTK from Control Center > Security > Antivirus.

input: How do I check my network speed?
output: Install speedtest-cli: sudo apt install speedtest-cli, then run: speedtest. Or open a browser and search for 'speed test' to use an online tool.

input: How do I set a static IP?
output: Open Control Center > Network, select your connection, go to IPv4 settings, and change from Automatic to Manual. Enter your IP address, gateway, and DNS servers.
Connect to a remote server: ssh user@hostname. Generate SSH keys: ssh-keygen -t ed25519. Copy key to server: ssh-copy-id user@hostname. TinkerOS has SSH configured by default.
Search for apps: flatpak search app-name. Install: flatpak install app-name. Run: flatpak run app-name. List installed: flatpak list. Update: flatpak update.
Download the .AppImage file, make it executable: chmod +x app.AppImage, then run it: ./app.AppImage. AppImages run without installation and can be stored anywhere.
TinkerOS has a custom Plymouth boot animation with a pulsing TinkerOS logo and progress bar. It shows during startup, shutdown, and reboot. The GRUB boot menu is also branded with the TinkerOS theme.

input: How do I change the boot theme?
output: Open Control Center > Customization > Boot Theme, or use: Plymouth theme: sudo plymouth-set-default-theme TinkerOS. For GRUB: sudo update-grub after making changes.

input: How do I access the BIOS?
output: Restart your computer and press the BIOS key during boot. Common keys: F2, F12, Del, Esc. The key depends on your motherboard manufacturer. TinkerOS will show a message during boot if you press Shift for GRUB.

input: How do I dual boot with Windows?
output: Install Windows first, then TinkerOS. During TinkerOS installation, choose 'Install alongside Windows'. The GRUB boot menu will let you choose between TinkerOS and Windows at startup.

input: How do I recover deleted files?
output: Check the Trash first. If emptied, try: sudo apt install testdisk && photorec. For git repos: git checkout HEAD -- filename. TinkerOS also has automatic backups if enabled.

input: How do I change the default browser?
output: Open Control Center > System > Default Applications, and select your preferred browser. Or use: xdg-settings set default-web-browser browser.desktop.

input: How do I add a keyboard shortcut?
output: Open Control Center > Customization > Keyboard Shortcuts. Click 'Add Shortcut', press your desired key combination, and assign it to an action or command.
Open Control Center > System > Users, select your user, and enable 'Automatic Login'. Be aware this reduces security if others have physical access to your computer.

input: How do I check system logs?
output: Use journalctl for system logs: journalctl -xe for recent errors, journalctl -u service-name for specific services. Or open Control Center > System > Logs for a GUI viewer.

input: How do I use the clipboard history?
output: Press Ctrl+V to paste, or Super+V to open the clipboard history panel. TinkerOS keeps a history of your copied items so you can paste older items.

input: How do I use multiple monitors?
output: Connect your monitors, then open Control Center > Display. You can arrange them, set resolution, and choose between mirror or extend mode. Or use: xrandr to configure from terminal.

input: How do I record my screen?
output: Type gnome-screenshot for screenshots, or use OBS Studio for video recording. Install OBS: sudo apt install obs-studio. It's available in the Software Center too.

input: How do I use virtual desktops?
output: Press Super+Tab to switch between virtual desktops. Create new ones with Super+Ctrl+Up. Move windows between desktops by dragging them to the edge of the screen.

input: How do I enable do not disturb?
output: Click the clock in the top bar to open the calendar panel, then toggle 'Do Not Disturb'. This silences all notifications until you turn it off.

input: How do I use night light?
output: Open Control Center > Display > Night Light and enable it. It reduces blue light in the evening to help you sleep better. You can set the schedule and color temperature.

input: How do I manage startup apps?
output: Open Control Center > System > Startup Applications. You can add, remove, or disable apps that start automatically when you log in.

input: How do I check my IP address?
output: Type ip addr show in the terminal, or hostname -I for a quick view. Open Control Center > Network to see your IP in the GUI.

input: How do I open a specific file?
output: Use the file manager (nautilus or thunar), or type: xdg-open filename in the terminal. TinkerAI can also open files for you: tinker-ai open filename.

input: How do I change the wallpaper?
output: Right-click the desktop and select 'Change Wallpaper', or open Control Center > Customization > Appearance. TinkerOS includes several glassmorphism-themed wallpapers.

input: How do I enable touchpad gestures?
output: Touchpad gestures are enabled by default. Use three-finger swipe up for activities, three-finger swipe left/right to switch desktops, and pinch to zoom in supported apps.

input: How do I use screen sharing?
output: Install Zoom or Teams from the Software Center, or use the built-in GNOME Screen Sharing. Open Control Center > System > Screen Sharing to enable remote access.

input: How do I manage my power settings?
output: Open Control Center > System > Power. You can set screen timeout, sleep timeout, and power button behavior. For more options, use: tinker-power save or tinker-power performance.

input: How do I check my GPU?
output: Type lspci | grep VGA in the terminal. For NVIDIA GPUs: nvidia-smi. For detailed info: glxinfo | grep 'OpenGL renderer'. Open Control Center > Hardware > Graphics for more.

input: How do I install NVIDIA drivers?
output: Open Control Center > Hardware > Graphics, or use: sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall. For specific version: sudo apt install nvidia-driver-535. Restart after installation.
TinkerOS supports Wayland by default. If you need X11, select 'GNOME on Xorg' at the login screen. Most apps work on Wayland; check compatibility for specialized tools.

input: How do I use fractional scaling?
output: For HiDPI displays: Settings > Displays > Scale. Choose 125%, 150%, or 175%. Or use: gsettings set org.gnome.mutter experimental-features "['scale-monitor-framebuffer']" for more options.

input: How do I enable location services?
output: Open Control Center > Privacy > Location Services and enable it. Apps like weather and maps can then use your approximate location for better results.

input: How do I manage app permissions?
output: Open Control Center > Privacy. You can control which apps have access to camera, microphone, location, files, and contacts. Toggle permissions per app.

input: How do I use parental controls?
output: Open Control Center > Parental Controls. You can set screen time limits, block inappropriate content, and manage which apps children can use.

input: How do I use the built-in backup?
output: Type tinker-backup in the terminal, or open Control Center > System > Backup. You can back up to an external drive, network location, or configure automatic backups.

input: How do I restore from backup?
output: Open Control Center > System > Backup > Restore, or use: tinker-backup restore in the terminal. Select your backup file and follow the wizard to restore your data.

input: How do I check my system specs?
output: Type neofetch in the terminal for a quick overview. Or use: lscpu for CPU, free -h for RAM, lsblk for disks, lspci for hardware. Open Control Center > Hardware > System Info for a GUI.

input: How do I overclock my CPU?
output: Open Control Center > Hardware > CPU > Overclocking. Be careful — overclocking can cause instability and overheating. TinkerOS monitors temperatures and will throttle if things get too hot.

input: How do I undervolt my CPU?
output: Use: sudo intel-undervolt apply in the terminal, or configure through Control Center > Hardware > CPU > Power. Undervolting reduces power consumption and heat while maintaining performance.

input: How do I check my SSD health?
output: Type: sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda in the terminal. Look for 'Reallocated Sector Count' and 'Wear Leveling'. Open Control Center > Hardware > Storage for a visual health display.

input: How do I enable TRIM for SSD?
output: TRIM is enabled by default on TinkerOS. Verify with: systemctl status fstrim.timer. If not running: sudo systemctl enable --now fstrim.timer.

input: How do I use ZFS on TinkerOS?
output: Install ZFS: sudo apt install zfsutils-linux. Create a pool: sudo zpool create tank /dev/sdb. Create datasets: sudo zfs create tank/data. ZFS provides snapshots, compression, and data integrity.

LVM is available during installation. For existing installs: sudo apt install lvm2. Create physical volumes: sudo pvcreate /dev/sdb. Create volume group: sudo vgcreate data /dev/sdb. Create logical volumes: sudo lvcreate -n backup -L 50G data.
TinkerOS supports software RAID through mdadm. Install: sudo apt install mdadm. Create array: sudo mdadm --create /dev/md0 --level=1 --raid-devices=2 /dev/sdb /dev/sdc. Monitor: cat /proc/mdstat.

input: How do I use the firewall?
output: TinkerOS uses UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall). Enable: sudo ufw enable. Allow SSH: sudo ufw allow ssh. Check status: sudo ufw status. Block an IP: sudo ufw deny from IP.
Install: sudo apt install fail2ban. Enable: sudo systemctl enable --now fail2ban. It automatically bans IPs with too many failed login attempts. Check banned IPs: sudo fail2ban-client status.

input: How do I use encryption for files?
output: Use GPG: gpg -c filename to encrypt, gpg filename.gpg to decrypt. For full disk encryption, choose the option during TinkerOS installation. For USB drives: veracrypt or luksFormat.
Install: sudo apt install tor. Start: sudo systemctl start tor. Configure browser to use SOCKS5 proxy at 127.0.0.1:9050. Or install Tor Browser from the Software Center.

input: How do I use a VPN?
output: Open Control Center > Network > VPN. Click Add VPN and enter your provider details. Or install: sudo apt install network-manager-openvpn-gnome for OpenVPN support.

input: How do I check for rootkits?
output: Install: sudo apt install rkhunter chkrootkit. Run: sudo rkhunter --check, or sudo chkrootkit. Schedule regular scans with cron for automatic detection.
Install: sudo apt install clamav clamav-daemon. Update definitions: sudo freshclam. Scan: sudo clamscan -r /home. Real-time protection: sudo systemctl enable --now clamav-daemon.

AppArmor is enabled by default. Check status: sudo aa-status. Enforce a profile: sudo aa-enforce /etc/apparmor.d/profile-name. Disable: sudo ln -s /etc/apparmor.d/profile-name /etc/apparmor.d/disable/.
SELinux is not the default on TinkerOS (it uses AppArmor). If needed: sudo apt install selinux-basics selinux-policy-default. Configure: sudo selinux-activate.

input: How do I use audit logs?
output: Install: sudo apt install auditd. Monitor files: sudo auditctl -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k password-changes. View logs: sudo ausearch -k password-changes. Report: sudo aureport.
Check services: systemctl list-units. Start/stop: sudo systemctl start/stop service. Enable at boot: sudo systemctl enable service. View logs: journalctl -u service.

input: How do I use cron jobs?
output: Edit crontab: crontab -e. Add a job: 0 9 * * * /path/to/script. Syntax: minute hour day month weekday command. List jobs: crontab -l. Remove all: crontab -r.
Edit ~/.bashrc and add: alias ll='ls -la'. Reload: source ~/.bashrc. Or add to ~/.bash_aliases for cleaner organization. Common aliases: ls, grep, update, upgrade.

input: How do I use environment variables?
output: Set temporarily: export MY_VAR=value. Set permanently: add to ~/.bashrc. View all: env or printenv. View specific: echo $MY_VAR. Unset: unset MY_VAR.

input: How do I use SSH keys?
output: Generate: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'your@email.com'. Copy to server: ssh-copy-id user@server. Connect: ssh user@server (no password needed). Keys are more secure than passwords.
Sync folders: rsync -avz /source/ /dest/. Preview: rsync -avzn /source/ /dest/. Exclude: rsync -avz --exclude='*.log' /source/ /dest/. Remote: rsync -avz /source/ user@host:/dest/.
Open file: vim filename. Insert mode: i. Save and quit: Esc then :wq. Quit without save: Esc then :q!. Delete line: dd. Search: /pattern. Vim is pre-installed on TinkerOS.
Search in file: grep 'pattern' filename. Recursive search: grep -r 'pattern' directory. Case insensitive: grep -i 'pattern' file. Show line numbers: grep -n 'pattern' file.
Find files: find /path -name 'filename'. Find by type: find . -type f -name '*.txt'. Find by size: find . -size +100M. Find modified today: find . -mtime 0.
Replace text: sed -i 's/old/new/g' filename. Delete lines: sed -i '/pattern/d' file. Insert line: sed -i '3a\new line' file. View without editing: sed 's/old/new/g' file.
Print column: awk '{print $1}' file. Filter: awk '$3 > 100' file. Custom delimiter: awk -F: '{print $1}' /etc/passwd. Combine: awk '{sum+=$1} END {print sum}' file.
Download: curl -O URL. POST data: curl -d 'data' URL. Follow redirects: curl -L URL. Save output: curl -o file URL. With headers: curl -H 'Header: Value' URL.
Download: wget URL. Recursive download: wget -r URL. Limit speed: wget --limit-rate=200k URL. Resume: wget -c URL. Background: wget -b URL.
Create archive: tar -czf archive.tar.gz folder/. Extract: tar -xzf archive.tar.gz. List contents: tar -tzf archive.tar.gz. Extract to specific dir: tar -xzf archive.tar.gz -C /path/.
Create: zip -r archive.zip folder/. Extract: unzip archive.zip. List contents: unzip -l archive.zip. Extract to dir: unzip archive.zip -d /path/.
Build project: make. Install: sudo make install. Clean: make clean. Specific target: make target. Read Makefile first to understand available targets.
Create build dir: mkdir build && cd build. Configure: cmake .. Build: make. Install: sudo make install. Clean: rm -rf build/ and start over.

input: How do I use docker compose?
output: Start services: docker-compose up -d. Stop: docker-compose down. View logs: docker-compose logs. Rebuild: docker-compose up --build. List services: docker-compose ps.
Apply config: kubectl apply -f file.yaml. Get pods: kubectl get pods. Describe: kubectl describe pod name. Logs: kubectl logs pod-name. Delete: kubectl delete -f file.yaml.

input: How do I create a git repository?
output: Initialize: git init. Add files: git add .. First commit: git commit -m 'initial commit'. Add remote: git remote add origin URL. Push: git push -u origin main.

input: How do I resolve merge conflicts?
output: Open conflicting files and look for <<<<<<, =======, =======. Choose which changes to keep, delete the conflict markers, then: git add filename && git commit.

input: How do I use git branches?
output: Create: git branch branch-name. Switch: git checkout branch-name. Create and switch: git checkout -b branch-name. List: git branch. Delete: git branch -d branch-name.
Run script: python3 script.py. Interactive: python3. Install packages: pip install package. Create virtual env: python3 -m venv env && source env/bin/activate.
Run script: node script.js. Install packages: npm install package. Init project: npm init. Start server: node server.js. Use npx for one-off commands.
Install: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh. Create project: cargo new project. Build: cargo build. Run: cargo run.
Install: sudo snap install go --classic. Create project: mkdir project && cd project && go mod init project. Build: go build. Run: go run main.go.
Install: sudo apt install mysql-server. Secure: sudo mysql_secure_installation. Login: mysql -u root -p. Create database: CREATE DATABASE name; Use: USE name;
Install: sudo apt install postgresql. Login: sudo -u postgres psql. Create database: CREATE DATABASE name; Create user: CREATE USER name WITH PASSWORD 'pass';
Install: sudo apt install redis-server. Start: sudo systemctl start redis. Connect: redis-cli. Set value: SET key value. Get value: GET key. List keys: KEYS *.
Install: sudo apt install nginx. Start: sudo systemctl start nginx. Config: /etc/nginx/sites-available/default. Test: nginx -t. Reload: sudo systemctl reload nginx.
Install: sudo apt install apache2. Start: sudo systemctl start apache2. Config: /etc/apache2/sites-available/. Enable site: sudo a2ensite site.conf. Reload: sudo systemctl reload apache2.
Config in /etc/logrotate.d/. Example: /var/log/app.log { daily rotate 7 compress }. Test: logrotate -d config. Force rotation: logrotate -f config.
Start: screen -S name. List: screen -ls. Attach: screen -r name. Detach: Ctrl+A then D. Kill: screen -X -S name quit. Split: Ctrl+A then S.
Start: byobu. New window: F2. Switch windows: F3/F4. Detach: F6. Status bar: F12. Byobu is an enhanced screen/tmux wrapper pre-installed on TinkerOS.
Switch default: chsh -s /bin/zsh. Install oh-my-zsh: sh -c '$(curl -fsSL https://raw.github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/master/tools/install.sh)'. Config: ~/.zshrc.
Install: sudo apt install fzf. Use: type ** then Tab for fuzzy completion. Search history: Ctrl+R. Search files: find . | fzf. Kill process: kill $(ps aux | fzf).
Install: sudo apt install ripgrep. Search: rg 'pattern' directory. Case insensitive: rg -i 'pattern'. File types: rg -t py 'pattern'. Replace: rg 'old' -r 'new' file.
Install: sudo apt install fd-find. Find files: fd pattern. Find by extension: fd -e py. Find by type: fd -t d (directories). Ignore: fd --exclude node_modules.
Install: sudo apt install bat. View file: bat file.py. Line numbers: bat -n file.py. Language detect: bat --list-languages. Diff: bat --diff file1 file2.
Install: sudo apt install exa. List: exa. Tree: exa --tree. Long format: exa -l. Git status: exa -l --git. Sort by size: exa --sort=size.
Install: sudo apt install git-delta. Configure git: git config --global core.pager delta. View diffs: git diff. Features: syntax highlighting, line numbers, side-by-side.
Install: sudo apt install lazygit. Run: lazygit. Navigate with arrow keys. Stage files: Space. Commit: c. Push: P. Pull: p. Quit: q. It's a terminal UI for git.
Install: sudo apt install httpie. GET: http URL. POST: http POST URL name=john. Headers: http URL Authorization:Bearer token. JSON: http POST URL json:={"key":"value"}.
Install: sudo apt install jq. Pretty print: cat file.json | jq. Filter: jq '.name' file.json. Array: jq '.[0]' file.json. Multiple: jq '{name, age}' file.json.
Install: sudo snap install yq. Read: yq '.metadata.name' file.yaml. Write: yq -i '.key = "value"' file.yaml. Convert: yq -o json file.yaml. Delete: yq -i 'del(.key)' file.yaml.
Install: sudo apt install neovim. Open: nvim file. Insert: i. Save: :w. Quit: :q. Install plugins: use lazy.nvim or vim-plug. Config: ~/.config/nvim/init.lua.
Install: sudo apt install podman. Run: podman run -it ubuntu bash. Build: podman build -t name . Rootless: no sudo needed. Podman is a Docker alternative.
Install: sudo snap install terraform. Init: terraform init. Plan: terraform plan. Apply: terraform apply. Destroy: terraform destroy. State: terraform state list.
Install: sudo apt install ansible. Ping hosts: ansible all -m ping. Run playbook: ansible-playbook playbook.yml. Ad-hoc: ansible all -m shell -a 'uptime'.
Install: sudo apt install vagrant. Init: vagrant init ubuntu/bionic64. Start: vagrant up. SSH: vagrant ssh. Stop: vagrant halt. Destroy: vagrant destroy.
Edit crontab: crontab -e. Run daily at 9am: 0 9 * * * /path/to/script. Run every hour: 0 * * * * command. Run weekly: 0 9 * * 0 command. View: crontab -l.

input: How do I use systemd timers?
output: Create .timer and .service files in /etc/systemd/system/. Enable: sudo systemctl enable timer-name. Start: sudo systemctl start timer-name. Check: systemctl list-timers.

input: What is the version of TinkerOS?
output: TinkerOS v1.3.0 runs on Linux 6.x with 27 custom kernel modules. It uses a GNOME desktop with glassmorphism theming, is based on Ubuntu/Debian, and ships as a ~7.6 GB bootable ISO.

input: How do I check TinkerOS version?
output: Type tinker-version in the terminal, or check the 'About' section in Control Center > System. You can also view neofetch output for detailed version information.
TinkerOS uses the Dual Source License v1.0. Option A is public (open source), Option B is private (closed source). Both options are available at no fee.
TinkerOS is available as a bootable ISO (~7.6 GB) from SourceForge: https://sourceforge.net/projects/tinkeros/files/v1.3/TinkerOS-v1.3.iso/. Flash it to a USB drive and boot from it.
Flash the ISO to a USB drive using Balena Etcher or dd. Boot from the USB, follow the installer. You can install alongside Windows (dual boot) or use the entire disk.

input: How do I check TinkerOS world status?
output: Type tinker-world status in the terminal to see which world is currently active. You can also look at the world indicator in the top bar of your desktop.

input: How do I use panic wipe?
output: Press Space+Shift+Escape to trigger a panic wipe. This is an emergency feature that wipes sensitive data. Use with caution — it's irreversible.

NORMAL is the most protected world in TinkerOS. It's for everyday use — standard desktop with all productivity apps. It can find/hack the user but CANNOT be hacked. It has 14 territory tools including app-allowlist, biometric-lock, and vault-engine.

HACK is the world that protects the hacker while helping them hack. Only Tor Browser works here, and only safe approved apps may run. It includes 18 territory tools like amnesia-firewall, kill-switch, and threat-monitor.

GAME is the maximum performance gaming world. It sets CPU perf governor to max, enables low-latency scheduler, optimizes GPU/IO priority, and activates GameMode. It has 13 territory tools including gpu-lock, frame-pacing, and game-replay-ai.

input: How do I use territory tools?
output: Territory tools are pre-configured for each world. Access them through Control Center > Territory Tools, or run them from the terminal. Each world has its own set of tools optimized for that environment.

input: What territory tools are in GAME world?
output: GAME world has 13 tools: anticheat-consent, audio-focus, controller-haptics, frame-pacing, game-mode, game-replay-ai, game-studio, gpu-lock, latency-clean, lowlat-input, perf-tune, save-archiver, and spectator-box.

input: What territory tools are in HACK world?
output: HACK world has 18 tools: amnesia-firewall, app-guard, browser-gate, canary-honeypot, ephemeral-ram, gpu-pipeline, hack-defense, hack-gate, hack-mode, hack-ways, intent-hardware, kill-switch, masked-proc, panic-wipe, portal-sandbox, reverse-proxy, sdr-isolation, split-personality, supply-chain, threat-monitor.

input: What territory tools are in NORMAL world?
output: NORMAL world has 14 tools: app-allowlist, biometric-lock, canary-monitor, duress-alert, filevault2, gatekeeper2, identity-cloud, key-wallet, privacy-ledger, secure-mode, sip-guard, traffic-guard, vault-engine, zero-trust-config.

input: How do I use the zero latency input?
output: The zero_latency_input kernel module is active in GAME world. It provides ultra-low-latency input handling for gaming. It's automatic — no configuration needed when in GAME world.

input: How do I use OLED protection?
output: The oled_wear kernel module automatically shifts pixels to prevent burn-in on OLED screens. It's active by default. Check status in Control Center > Hardware > OLED Protection.

input: How do I use cache tiering?
output: The cache_tiering kernel module optimizes CPU cache usage automatically. It's active in all worlds. You can adjust settings in Control Center > Hardware > Cache Tiering.

input: How do I use thermal scheduling?
output: The thermal_sched kernel module manages smart thermal cooling with user hints. It's active by default. It adjusts fan speeds and CPU throttling based on temperature. Check in Control Center > Hardware > Thermal.

input: How do I use energy scheduling?
output: The energy_sched kernel module is a battery saver that adapts to your usage patterns. It's active in NORMAL world. It optimizes power consumption automatically.

input: How do I use coil whine reduction?
output: The coil_whine kernel module uses spread-spectrum technology to reduce coil whine noise. It's active by default. No configuration needed — it works silently in the background.

input: How do I calibrate the dust dislodger?
output: Before using the dust dislodger, calibrate it first: tinker-dust calibrate. This calculates the fan rated ceiling, RPM-per-PWM slope, and stall-floor for your specific hardware.

input: How do I use the hardware fingerprinting?
output: The hardware_dna kernel module fingerprints your hardware for security purposes. It's used by NORMAL world's security tools to verify system integrity. Check status in Control Center > Security > Hardware DNA.

input: How do I use software-defined GPU?
output: The sdgpu kernel module provides software-defined GPU capabilities. It allows dynamic GPU resource allocation. Configure through Control Center > Hardware > GPU > Software Defined.

input: How do I use FPGA scaler?
output: The fpga_scaler kernel module provides FPGA-based hardware scaling. It's an advanced feature for hardware acceleration. Configure through Control Center > Hardware > FPGA Scaler.

input: How do I use CXL memory?
output: The cxl_memory kernel module provides CXL (Compute Express Link) memory support. It's for systems with CXL-compatible hardware. Configure through Control Center > Hardware > CXL Memory.

input: How do I use predictive prewarm?
output: The predictive_prewarm kernel module intelligently preloads data based on usage patterns. It improves application launch times by predicting what you'll need. Active by default in all worlds.

input: How do I use smart power grid?
output: The smart_power_grid kernel module optimizes power distribution across system components. It balances performance and efficiency. Active by default — no manual configuration needed.

input: How do I use adaptive display?
output: The adaptive_display kernel module adjusts display settings based on content and environment. It optimizes brightness, contrast, and color temperature. Configure in Control Center > Display > Adaptive.

input: How do I use unified memory?
output: The unified_memory kernel module provides unified memory management across CPU and GPU. It improves data transfer efficiency for graphics-intensive tasks. Active in GAME world by default.

input: How do I use hardware tuning?
output: The hardware_tuning kernel module provides fine-grained hardware control. Access through Control Center > Hardware > Hardware Tuning. It allows adjusting CPU, GPU, and memory parameters.

input: How do I use neural super resolution?
output: The neural_super_res kernel module uses AI to upscale images and video in real-time. It improves visual quality without the performance cost of native resolution. Active in GAME world.

input: How do I use predictive rendering?
output: The predictive_render kernel module predicts and pre-renders upcoming frames to reduce latency. It's optimized for gaming in GAME world. Active automatically when gaming.

input: How do I use remote hardware API?
output: The remote_hardware_api kernel module allows remote access to hardware resources. It's for advanced users who need to control hardware remotely. Configure through Control Center > Advanced > Remote HW API.

input: How do I use finance audit?
output: The finance_audit kernel module provides financial data auditing capabilities. It's used by NORMAL world's vault-engine and privacy-ledger tools for secure financial tracking.

input: What is the capital of France?
output: The capital of France is Paris. It's the largest city in France and a major European hub for art, fashion, and culture.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose (food) and oxygen. It happens in the chloroplasts of plant cells.

input: What is the speed of light?
output: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second, or about 186,282 miles per second. It's the fastest speed possible in the universe.
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the molecule that carries genetic instructions for life. It's shaped like a double helix and contains the code that determines your traits.

Climate change refers to long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns. While natural cycles exist, human activities like burning fossil fuels have been the main driver since the 1800s.

input: What is the theory of relativity?
output: Einstein's theory of relativity says that space and time are connected (spacetime), and that gravity is the warping of spacetime by mass. It has two parts: special relativity (moving objects) and general relativity (gravity).
Artificial intelligence (AI) is computer software that can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, like understanding language, recognizing images, and making decisions.
Machine learning is a type of AI where computers learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed. It's used for predictions, recommendations, and recognizing patterns.
Quantum computing uses quantum mechanics (superposition and entanglement) to process information in fundamentally different ways than regular computers. They can solve certain problems much faster.
Blockchain is a distributed digital ledger that records transactions across many computers. It's the technology behind cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and ensures data can't be altered retroactively.
The internet is a global network of interconnected computers that communicate using standardized protocols. It enables email, websites, streaming, and billions of other services.
Python is a popular programming language known for its simplicity and readability. It's used for web development, data science, AI, automation, and scripting. Great for beginners.
Linux is an open-source operating system kernel created by Linus Torvalds in 1991. It's the foundation for distributions like Ubuntu, Debian, and TinkerOS. It powers most servers worldwide.
An API (Application Programming Interface) is a set of rules that lets different software programs communicate with each other. It defines what requests can be made and how responses are formatted.

Cloud computing is delivering computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking) over the internet. Instead of owning physical hardware, you rent computing power from providers like AWS or Azure.
The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².
Pi (π) is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, approximately 3.14159. It's an irrational number that goes on forever without repeating.

input: What is the formula for area of a circle?
output: The area of a circle is A = πr², where r is the radius. If you know the diameter, the radius is half the diameter.

A derivative measures the rate of change of a function at any point. It tells you the slope of the tangent line. In physics, it represents velocity (derivative of position) or acceleration (derivative of velocity).

An integral is the reverse of a derivative. It calculates the total accumulation of a quantity, like finding the area under a curve. The fundamental theorem of calculus connects derivatives and integrals.

input: What is the Internet of Things?
output: IoT refers to everyday objects (lights, thermostats, cars, appliances) connected to the internet, allowing them to send and receive data. Smart home devices are a common example.
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting systems, networks, and data from digital attacks. It includes firewalls, encryption, antivirus, and security practices to keep information safe.
Open source software has publicly available source code that anyone can view, modify, and distribute. Linux, Python, and Firefox are examples. It fosters collaboration and transparency.

input: What is a virus in computing?
output: A computer virus is malicious software that replicates itself by attaching to other programs. It can damage files, steal data, or disrupt system operations. Antivirus software helps detect and remove them.
A firewall is a security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined rules. It acts as a barrier between trusted and untrusted networks.
Encryption converts data into a coded format that can only be read with the correct key. It protects sensitive information during transmission or storage. Common types include AES and RSA.
SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to manage and query relational databases. Commands include SELECT (read data), INSERT (add data), UPDATE (modify data), and DELETE (remove data).
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication on the web. It defines how messages are formatted and transmitted between browsers and servers. HTTPS is the secure version.
DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names (like google.com) into IP addresses that computers use. It's like a phone book for the internet.
TCP/IP is the fundamental communication protocol of the internet. TCP handles reliable data delivery, and IP handles addressing and routing. Together they enable all internet communication.
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages. It uses tags to structure content like headings, paragraphs, links, and images.
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation of HTML elements. It handles colors, fonts, layouts, and responsive design. It makes web pages look good.
JavaScript is a programming language that runs in web browsers. It makes web pages interactive with features like animations, form validation, and dynamic content updates.
A database is an organized collection of structured data stored electronically. Examples include MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB. They're used by apps to store and retrieve information efficiently.
Version control tracks changes to files over time. Git is the most popular system. It lets you revert to previous versions, collaborate with others, and maintain a history of all changes.
Agile is a software development approach that delivers work in small, iterative increments. Teams work in short cycles (sprints), continuously improving based on feedback.
DevOps combines software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops) to shorten the development lifecycle. It emphasizes automation, continuous integration, and collaboration.

Microservices is an architecture where applications are built as small, independent services that communicate over APIs. Each service handles a specific function and can be developed, deployed, and scaled independently.
A container is a lightweight, standalone package of software that includes everything needed to run: code, runtime, libraries, and settings. Docker is the most popular container platform.
Kubernetes (K8s) is an open-source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. It orchestrates containers across multiple servers.
CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment. CI automatically builds and tests code when changes are pushed. CD automatically deploys validated code to production.
A load balancer distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers. It ensures no single server is overwhelmed, improving reliability and performance.
A CDN (Content Delivery Network) is a distributed network of servers that delivers web content based on the user's geographic location. It speeds up website loading times.
OAuth is an authentication protocol that allows third-party apps to access your data without sharing your password. When you 'Sign in with Google', that's OAuth in action.
A REST API is an architectural style for web services that uses HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to perform operations on resources identified by URLs. It's stateless and scalable.
GraphQL is a query language for APIs that lets clients request exactly the data they need. Unlike REST, it returns only the requested fields, reducing over-fetching and under-fetching.
WebSocket provides full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection. Unlike HTTP, it allows real-time bidirectional data transfer. Used for chat apps and live updates.
A proxy server acts as an intermediary between your computer and the internet. It can cache content, filter requests, hide your IP address, and improve security.
A VPN (Virtual Private Network) encrypts your internet connection and routes it through a server in another location. It protects your privacy and can bypass geographic restrictions.
Tor (The Onion Router) routes your internet traffic through multiple encrypted layers and volunteer servers worldwide, making it very difficult to trace your activity. It provides strong anonymity.
Cryptocurrency is digital money that uses cryptography for security and operates on decentralized networks (usually blockchain). Bitcoin and Ethereum are the most well-known examples.
The stock market is where shares of publicly traded companies are bought and sold. Prices are determined by supply and demand. Major indices include the S&P 500, Dow Jones, and NASDAQ.

Compound interest is interest calculated on both the initial principal and accumulated interest from previous periods. It makes savings grow faster over time. Einstein reportedly called it the eighth wonder of the world.

GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period. It's the most widely used measure of economic activity.
Inflation is the rate at which prices for goods and services increase over time, reducing purchasing power. Moderate inflation is normal in healthy economies, but high inflation erodes savings.
Supply and demand is the economic model of price determination. When demand exceeds supply, prices rise. When supply exceeds demand, prices fall. The equilibrium is where they meet.
Mitochondria are organelles found in most cells. They're known as the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell's ATP (energy currency) through cellular respiration.
Evolution is the process by which species change over time through natural selection. Organisms with traits better suited to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce.

Gravity is a fundamental force that attracts objects with mass toward each other. On Earth, it gives objects weight and causes them to fall when dropped. Einstein described it as curvature of spacetime.
Electricity is the flow of electric charge through a conductor. It powers our homes, devices, and technology. It can be generated from many sources including solar, wind, and fossil fuels.
An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains the properties of that element. It consists of a nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons. All matter is made of atoms.
The periodic table organizes all known chemical elements by their atomic number, electron configuration, and chemical properties. It was first developed by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.
pH is a measure of how acidic or basic a solution is, on a scale from 0 to 14. 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic. Pure water has a pH of 7.
Entropy is a measure of disorder or randomness in a system. The second law of thermodynamics says entropy in an isolated system always increases over time.
A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. They form when massive stars collapse at the end of their life cycle.
Renewable energy comes from sources that are naturally replenished: sunlight, wind, water, geothermal heat, and biomass. They produce little to no greenhouse gas emissions.
Recycling is the process of converting waste materials into new products. It reduces the need for raw materials, saves energy, and decreases landfill waste.

Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It balances economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental protection.

Deforestation is the clearing of forests for other land uses. It destroys habitats, releases carbon dioxide, and disrupts water cycles. The Amazon rainforest loses about 10,000 square kilometers per year.
Gravity is a fundamental force attracting objects with mass. On Earth, it accelerates objects at 9.8 m/s².
Light is electromagnetic radiation visible to humans, wavelength 380-700nm, traveling at 300,000 km/s.
Quantum mechanics studies behavior at atomic scales where particles exist in superposition and entanglement.
Einstein's theory linking space, time, and gravity. Special relativity deals with high speeds; general with gravity.
Energy is the capacity to do work, existing as kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, nuclear, and electromagnetic forms.
Matter has mass and occupies space. States: solid, liquid, gas, plasma, Bose-Einstein condensate.
Electricity is the flow of electric charge (electrons) through a conductor, driven by voltage differences.
Magnetism is a force from moving electric charges, creating fields that attract or repel materials.
Wavelength is the distance between wave crests, determining electromagnetic radiation type.
Frequency is wave cycles per second in Hertz. Higher frequency = more energy.
Nuclear fission splits heavy atomic nuclei into lighter ones, releasing energy (used in nuclear power).
Nuclear fusion combines light nuclei into heavier ones, releasing enormous energy (powers the Sun).
Friction is a force resisting relative motion between surfaces, converting kinetic energy to heat.
Inertia is an object's resistance to changes in motion, proportional to mass (Newton's First Law).
Velocity is speed with direction, a vector quantity. Formula: v = displacement/time.
Acceleration is the rate of velocity change, measured in m/s². a = (v-u)/t.
Momentum is mass times velocity (p=mv). It is conserved in closed systems.
Pressure is force per unit area (P=F/A), measured in Pascals. Atmospheric pressure is ~101,325 Pa.
Temperature measures average kinetic energy of particles. Scales: Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kelvin.
Absolute zero is -273.15°C (0 Kelvin), the theoretical lowest temperature where particles stop moving.
A photon is a quantum of light, a massless particle that carries electromagnetic force.
An electron is a subatomic particle with negative charge, orbiting the nucleus in atoms.
A proton is a positively charged subatomic particle in the atomic nucleus, with mass ~1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg.
A neutron is a neutral subatomic particle in the nucleus, with mass slightly greater than a proton.
Dark energy is a hypothetical form of energy causing the accelerated expansion of the universe (~68% of total energy).
The Higgs boson is a particle associated with the Higgs field, which gives other particles mass. Discovered in 2012.
Superconductivity is zero electrical resistance in certain materials below a critical temperature.
Wave-particle duality is the concept that particles exhibit both wave and particle properties.
Heisenberg's uncertainty principle: you cannot simultaneously know a particle's exact position and momentum.
Entropy is a measure of disorder in a system. The Second Law of Thermodynamics says entropy always increases.
An atom is the smallest unit of an element: nucleus (protons+neutrons) + electrons.
A molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
Water (H₂O) is two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
DNA carries genetic instructions as a double helix of nucleotides (A, T, G, C).
pH measures acidity: 0-7 acidic, 7 neutral, 7-14 basic. pH = -log[H⁺].
An element is a pure substance of one atom type. 118 known elements on the periodic table.
Chemical bonds hold atoms together: ionic (electron transfer), covalent (electron sharing), metallic.
Carbon (element 6) forms 4 bonds, basis of organic chemistry. Exists as diamond, graphite, graphene.
Isotopes are variants of an element with same protons but different neutrons.
A catalyst speeds up chemical reactions without being consumed.
Oxidation is loss of electrons. Rust is iron oxidizing. Anti-oxidants prevent oxidation in food/body.
A polymer is a large molecule made of repeating subunits. Examples: plastic, DNA, rubber.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute dissolved in solvent (e.g., salt in water).
An acid donates hydrogen ions (H⁺) in solution, has pH < 7, and tastes sour.
A base accepts hydrogen ions (H⁺), has pH > 7, and feels slippery.
The periodic table organizes 118 elements by atomic number, groups (columns), and periods (rows).
The electron cloud is the region around the nucleus where electrons are likely to be found.
A covalent bond shares electron pairs between atoms, forming molecules.
An ionic bond transfers electrons between atoms, creating charged ions that attract.
Quantum chemistry applies quantum mechanics to chemical systems and molecular behavior.
A cell is the basic unit of life. Types: prokaryotic (no nucleus) and eukaryotic (has nucleus).
Evolution is change in inherited traits over generations through natural selection and mutation.
Plants convert sunlight + water + CO₂ → glucose + oxygen using chlorophyll.
The immune system defends against infections using white blood cells, antibodies, and inflammation.
A gene is a DNA segment encoding instructions for a protein or function.
Organisms with advantageous traits survive and reproduce more, passing those traits to offspring.
Mitosis produces two identical daughter cells from one parent cell (growth/repair).
Meiosis produces four genetically unique sex cells (gametes) with half the chromosomes.
Osmosis is water movement through a semi-permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration.
Chromosomes are DNA-protein structures carrying genes. Humans have 46 (23 pairs).
A virus is a non-living infectious agent requiring a host cell to replicate. Smaller than bacteria.
Bacteria are single-celled prokaryotic organisms. Some cause disease; most are harmless or beneficial.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Carbon dioxide and water become glucose and oxygen.
Cells break down glucose to produce ATP energy: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP.
DNA replication copies the double helix using helicase, primase, DNA polymerase, and ligase.
DNA → mRNA (transcription) → ribosome → protein (translation). Amino acids chain into polypeptides.
Light-dependent reactions split water (in thylakoids). Calvin cycle fixes CO₂ (in stroma).
The circulatory system transports blood via heart, arteries, veins, and capillaries.
The nervous system uses neurons to transmit signals between brain, spinal cord, and body.

output: Variation + inheritance + differential survival = evolution. First described by Darwin and Wallace.
Genetics studies heredity and variation of traits through genes and DNA.
An ecosystem is a community of organisms interacting with their physical environment.
Biodiversity is the variety of life in an ecosystem or on Earth, crucial for ecosystem resilience.
Symbiosis is close interaction between species: mutualism (both benefit), commensalism, parasitism.
Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions in an organism (temperature, pH, etc.).
A black hole is where gravity is so strong nothing escapes. Formed from collapsed massive stars.
The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star, 4.6 billion years old, containing 99.86% of solar system mass.
A light-year is 9.46 trillion km — the distance light travels in one year.
Dark matter doesn't emit light but has mass, causing gravitational effects on galaxies.
The universe began 13.8 billion years ago from an infinitely hot, dense point that expanded.

A neutron star is the collapsed core of a massive star. A teaspoon weighs ~6 billion tons.
Earth's only natural satellite, 384,400 km away, causing tides and stabilizing Earth's axial tilt.
A constellation is a pattern of stars in the sky, named after mythological figures or objects.
The Sun + 8 planets + dwarf planets + moons + asteroids + comets, formed ~4.6 billion years ago.
Mars is the fourth planet, the 'Red Planet' due to iron oxide. Has the tallest volcano (Olympus Mons).
Jupiter is the largest planet, a gas giant with the Great Red Spot (a storm larger than Earth).
Saturn is famous for its rings of ice and rock. It's the second-largest planet.
A comet is an icy body that orbits the Sun, developing a tail of gas and dust when near the Sun.
An asteroid is a rocky body orbiting the Sun, mostly found in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
The Milky Way is our galaxy, a barred spiral ~100,000 light-years across containing our solar system.
A pulsar is a rapidly rotating neutron star emitting beams of electromagnetic radiation.
A quasar is an extremely luminous active galactic nucleus powered by a supermassive black hole.
The habitable zone is the orbit around a star where liquid water can exist on a planet's surface.
An exoplanet orbits a star outside our solar system. Thousands have been discovered since 1995.
An algorithm is a finite set of step-by-step instructions for solving a problem or accomplishing a task.
ML lets systems learn from data to improve without explicit programming. Types: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement.
AI simulates human intelligence by machines, including learning, reasoning, problem-solving, and perception.
A neural network uses layers of interconnected nodes inspired by biological brains to process information.
Cloud computing delivers servers, storage, databases, and software over the internet on a pay-as-you-go basis.
Cybersecurity protects systems, networks, and data from digital attacks and unauthorized access.
Blockchain is a distributed ledger recording transactions across many computers, making records immutable.
Open source software has publicly available source code anyone can inspect, modify, and distribute.
An API (Application Programming Interface) lets different software applications communicate with each other.
Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem.
Big data refers to extremely large datasets that require advanced tools to process and analyze.
IoT (Internet of Things) connects physical devices to the internet for data collection and control.
Edge computing processes data near the source instead of in a centralized cloud, reducing latency.
Virtualization creates virtual versions of servers, storage, or networks to share physical resources.
Containerization packages applications with dependencies for consistent deployment (Docker, Kubernetes).
Quantum computing uses qubits that can be 0 and 1 simultaneously, solving certain problems exponentially faster.
Deep learning uses multi-layered neural networks to learn complex patterns from large datasets.
NLP enables computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information from images and videos.
Reinforcement learning trains agents by rewarding desired behaviors in an environment.
A data structure is a way to organize and store data for efficient access (arrays, trees, graphs, hash tables).
OOP organizes code into classes and objects, using encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.
Functional programming treats computation as evaluation of mathematical functions, avoiding mutable state.
A compiler translates entire source code into machine code before execution (vs. interpreter which does it line by line).
Garbage collection automatically reclaims memory occupied by objects no longer referenced by the program.
A hash function maps input data to fixed-size output, used in密码学, databases, and checksums.
Sorting arranges data in order. Common algorithms: bubble sort, merge sort, quicksort, heapsort.
Binary search finds an element in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. O(log n).
Dynamic programming solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing results.
Graph algorithms traverse and analyze graph structures: BFS, DFS, Dijkstra's, Bellman-Ford.
Computers connect via cables/wireless/satellite using TCP/IP protocol to send data packets.
HTTP is the protocol for web communication. HTTPS adds encryption via TLS/SSL.

HTML defines web page structure with tags like
,

CSS styles web pages: colors, layouts, fonts, responsive design. Selectors target HTML elements.
JavaScript adds interactivity to websites. Runs in browsers and servers (Node.js).
A domain name (like google.com) maps to an IP address via DNS.
DNS translates domain names to IP addresses, like a phone book for the internet.
WiFi uses radio waves (2.4GHz/5GHz/6GHz) for wireless networking over short distances.
A web browser renders HTML/CSS/JS. Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge are popular browsers.
Streaming transmits data continuously for real-time audio/video playback without full download.
A CDN distributes content across global servers, reducing latency by serving users from nearby locations.
SEO optimizes websites to rank higher in search engine results through content and technical improvements.
Responsive design makes websites adapt to different screen sizes using flexible layouts and media queries.
A web server stores and serves web content. Apache, Nginx, and LiteSpeed are popular servers.
SSL/TLS encrypts data between browsers and servers. The padlock icon indicates a secure HTTPS connection.
A cookie is a small data file stored by websites in your browser to remember preferences and sessions.
A session maintains user state across multiple HTTP requests (e.g., keeping you logged in).
REST APIs use HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to interact with resources via URLs.
GraphQL is a query language for APIs letting clients request exactly the data they need.
WebSocket enables full-duplex communication between client and server over a single TCP connection.
The CPU executes instructions. Modern CPUs have multiple cores, cache levels, and clock speeds in GHz.
RAM is volatile memory for active data. DDR4/DDR5 types. More RAM = more concurrent applications.
A GPU renders graphics and accelerates parallel computations (AI, crypto mining, scientific computing).
An SSD uses flash memory for storage, much faster and more durable than HDDs.
An HDD stores data on spinning magnetic platters. Cheaper per GB but slower than SSDs.
The motherboard connects all components: CPU socket, RAM slots, PCIe slots, storage connectors.
The kernel is the OS core managing hardware resources and providing services for applications.
Linux is an open-source OS kernel by Linus Torvalds (1991), powering servers, Android, and supercomputers.
An OS manages hardware/software resources. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.
BIOS/UEFI initializes hardware during boot and provides runtime services to the OS.
A driver is software that lets the OS communicate with hardware devices.
PCIe is a high-speed interface for connecting GPUs, SSDs, and other expansion cards.
USB (Universal Serial Bus) connects peripherals. Versions: 1.0 to 4.0, speeds from 1.5Mbps to 40Gbps.
Thunderbolt combines PCIe and DisplayPort in one interface. Thunderbolt 4 runs at 40Gbps.

Cricket: bat and ball sport, two teams of 11, batting and bowling on an oval field.
Golf: hit a ball into a hole using fewest strokes possible over 18 holes.
Swimming: competitive races in butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle.
The Olympics: international multi-sport event every 4 years, Summer and Winter editions.
A marathon is a 42.195 km (26.2 miles) long-distance running race.
Rugby: two teams of 15 (or 7s variant), oval ball, score by tries (5 pts) and kicks.
Hockey: field hockey or ice hockey, two teams score by hitting a ball/puck into a goal.
Boxing: combat sport, two fighters throw punches in a ring for rounds.
Mixed Martial Arts combines techniques from boxing, wrestling, jiu-jitsu, and other combat sports.
Formula 1: premier auto racing series with the fastest road-course racing cars.
Cycling: road racing, track, mountain bike, BMX. Tour de France is the most famous race.
Table tennis (ping pong): two or four players hit a lightweight ball back and forth across a table.
Badminton: racket sport hitting a shuttlecock over a net. Fastest racket sport (400+ km/h smashes).
Volleyball: two teams of 6 hit a ball over a net, scoring when the ball hits the opponent's court.
Skateboarding: riding and performing tricks on a skateboard. Olympic sport since 2020.

input: In Clean Architecture, what does the Dependency Inversion Principle dictate?
output: Source code dependencies must point inward toward high-level policies and business logic. Inner circles contain domain logic, and outer mechanisms like databases and UIs must depend on abstractions of the inner circles.

input: What is the primary function of the Circuit Breaker pattern in microservice architectures?
output: A circuit breaker prevents an application from continually trying to execute an operation that is likely to fail. It fails fast when a downstream service is down, preventing cascading failures.

input: In the Raft consensus algorithm, how is the leader determined?
output: Candidates receive votes from a majority of nodes during randomized timeout elections. Raft uses randomized election timeouts to trigger leader elections, requiring a majority quorum vote.

input: What does Sartre mean by existence precedes essence?
output: Humans are born first without a predefined purpose, and they define their own meaning through choices. Unlike a manufactured object whose purpose precedes its existence, humans exist first and craft their essence through actions.

input: How does Sisyphus achieve happiness in Camus's Myth of Sisyphus?
output: By fully accepting the absurdity of his fate and owning the struggle as his own. By recognizing his fate and taking ownership of the rock, Sisyphus turns his condemnation into a conscious act of rebellion.

input: What characterizes Nietzsche's concept of the Übermensch?
output: An individual who creates their own intrinsic values and overcomes conventional herd morality. The Übermensch moves beyond slave morality to actively affirm life and legislate self-determined values.

input: According to Kierkegaard, what role does angst or dread play?
output: Angst is the dizziness of freedom, revealing the immense possibility of choice and responsibility. Dread is the realization that we are free to choose, confronting us with the weight of possibility.

input: What does Heidegger's term Dasein signify?
output: The specific human mode of being characterized by being-there and engagement with the world. Dasein refers to human existence as inherently situated and relational within the world.

input: What is the difference between demand-pull and cost-push inflation?
output: Demand-pull is driven by an increase in aggregate demand (too much money chasing too few goods), whereas cost-push is driven by a decrease in aggregate supply due to higher input costs.

input: Who implements fiscal policy and what are its main tools?
output: The government (legislative and executive branches) implements fiscal policy using taxation and public spending as its main tools.

input: What does the Phillips Curve illustrate?
output: An inverse trade-off where lower unemployment is associated with higher inflation. As policy drives down unemployment, aggregate demand pushes inflation up.

A country should specialize in producing goods where it has the lowest opportunity cost, even if another country is more efficient at everything. Trade benefits all nations when they specialize based on comparative opportunity costs.

input: How is GDP calculated using the expenditure approach?
output: Consumer spending + business investment + government purchases + net exports (C + I + G + NX).

input: What is the primary function of a GFCI outlet?
output: To instantly cut off power when an imbalance in current is detected between the hot and neutral wires, preventing electrocution. GFCIs monitor current flow and trip within milliseconds if electricity leaks.

input: Why should you flush a water heater periodically?
output: To remove sediment and mineral buildup that reduces heating efficiency and damages the tank bottom. Minerals settle at the bottom, creating a barrier between the burner and water.

input: What happens with an excessively high MERV filter in HVAC?

input: Which fire extinguisher class is for kitchen grease fires?

input: What is the benefit of weatherstripping on exterior doors?
output: To reduce air infiltration and drafts, improving thermal comfort and lowering energy bills. Air gaps around doors leak conditioned air out and outdoor air in.

input: What is Amabile's Componential Model of Creativity?
output: Creativity requires the confluence of domain-relevant skills, creativity-relevant processes, and intrinsic task motivation. All three components must intersect for high creative output.

input: What is Mednick's Associative Theory of Creativity?
output: A steep associative hierarchy has one dominant response blocking alternative associations, whereas a flat hierarchy has multiple equiprobable weak associations accessible for novel combinations.

input: How do automatic stabilizers work in recession?

input: Why prefer Conditional Cash Transfers over unconditional?

input: How does a Pigouvian tax achieve efficiency?

input: What are ipRGCs and their role in circadian rhythm?

input: How does NEAT differ from TEF and BMR?

input: What limits the ATP-PC energy system?

input: How does Goodhart's Law manifest in software development metrics?
